Task: Fix trailing-average calculation for hourly sampling
Detailed Instructions: Fixed in update_history(): the hourly multi-origin pipeline calls this function roughly once/hour, but the old same-day branch simply overwrote today's stored price with whatever the LATEST fetch saw -- if price ticked up later in the day, a genuinely cheaper earlier-today price was silently discarded, understating that day's real cheapest fare and subtly corrupting every hourly-pipeline route's trailing average. Now takes min(existing, new) for same-day updates -- the same 'cheapest wins' principle cheapest_result() already applies within one fetch, extended across a full day's worth of hourly fetches. The once-daily JFK pipeline was never affected (only ever calls this once/day).
Link / Resource: Phase 1 Deal Ranking Script (Step 9 - with fallback).py
Notes: Verified with a standalone functional test (3 same-day calls at $500/$300/$400 -- confirmed the stored value stays at $300, the minimum, not $400 from the last call) and by running the full fixed script against copies of the real production data files (both daily and hourly pipelines) -- no crashes, sane output. Real committed data files were NOT regenerated/touched -- the bug never corrupted stored data structurally (unlike the earlier double-prefix bug), it just could store a non-minimal same-day price, which self-corrects naturally once the fixed code runs on its next scheduled cycle. No manual data surgery needed. A SECOND, more significant self-bias bug was found while regenerating real data for Step 96 (see that row): classify_destination() loads history BEFORE calling update_history() within one run, but ACROSS multiple same-day runs (the hourly pipeline's whole point), a run after the first one that day would load history that ALREADY included today's own price from the earlier run -- violating the function's own documented 'today's own price must never bias the average' rule. Fixed by excluding today's date from the history classify_destination() reads, unconditionally. Verified by simulating two same-day classify_destination() calls with update_history() run between them -- confirmed trailing_avg and history_points now stay identical across both calls, not drifting. Confirmed stable against real production data too: two consecutive same-day regenerations of all three pipelines (daily, hourly, other-origins) now produce byte-for-byte identical output, where before this second fix they didn't.

Detailed Instructions: Fixed in apply_fallback(): there was no upper bound on how long a stale 'last known price' could keep being carried forward -- a route with no fresh data would display the same old price indefinitely, potentially for months, as if it were still current. Beyond 7 days (or if last_fresh_date is missing/malformed -- fails safe), the fallback is no longer used at all; the route falls through as insufficient_history/no_data instead of showing a stale price with a live 'Book this fare' CTA.
